title: Multi-GPU stability prober for pipeline+tensor sync and p95 regression detection
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a repeatable harness that probes multi-GPU pipeline+tensor-parallel inference topologies for stability regressions and p95 latency drift. The prober will synthesize workloads across sequence-length mixes, token emission patterns (steady vs microburst), and KV-cache states (cold, warmed, partial warm) to measure tokens/sec and p95 under realistic production mixes and to generate automated regression alerts when baseline deviations exceed thresholds.
background: We have a number of existing throughput benchmarks but observed gaps: (1) regressions that only show up under interleaved seqlen mixes, (2) flakiness when PP and TP are combined across heterogeneous nodes, and (3) p95 drift after long-lived KV cache warmups. Existing harnesses focus on peak throughput; we need a stability-focused prober that emphasizes p95 and regression sensitivity for real application patterns.
proposed_solution: Implement a portable harness compatible with our existing perf infra that drives configurable scenarios across TP/PP meshes. Key features: scenario templating (seq len distribution, microburst frequency, kv-warmup ratio), fault-injection knobs (single-rank CPU/GPU preemption, slow-allreduce), per-request tracing for latency breakdowns, automated baseline comparison and regression scoring, and integration with Grafana + Alertmanager for noisy-but-actionable alerts. Output artifacts: time-series metrics (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, error-rate), event traces, and a run-level JSON summary suitable for our regression detector pipeline.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for scenario templates and result serializers. 2) Run harness across three canonical topologies: small-TP(2)-PP(1), mid-TP(4)-PP(2), and large-TP(8)-PP(4) using both homogeneous and heterogeneous GPU mixes. 3) Inject slow-allreduce and single-rank preemption during the steady-state window and confirm detection. 4) Validate p95 drift detection by running a synthetic baseline and then introducing a 12% latency regression; ensure detector flags and creates a regression ticket. 5) Post-run, verify Grafana dashboards update and Alertmanager fires a grouped alert with links to the run JSON and trace.
metrics: tokens_per_second, latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, error_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, allreduce_time_ms
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run headlessly in CI and on perf cluster with a single CLI command
Produces run-level JSON summarizing metrics and trace links for every run
Regression detector config flags deviations >10% p95 or >15% drop tokens/sec compared to baseline
Alerts include run id, topology, seqlen mix, and a minimal triage checklist
No false positives in the canonical stable baseline runs (3 consecutive stable runs)
steps: Design scenario template schema and CLI options
Implement workload generator that drives request patterns and supports KV-cache warmup control
Wire per-request tracing hooks and serialize traces to S3-compatible perf storage
Add fault injection layer talking to cluster orchestration (simulate CPU/GPU preempt and network delay)
Implement baseline comparison and regression scoring logic and integrate with Alertmanager/Grafana
Create dashboards and a standardized run JSON spec and document usage in Confluence
Run end-to-end validation across canonical topologies and iterate on thresholds
notes: We should reuse existing serializers from ENG-30412 and reuse the saturation matrix kernels where possible. Coordinate with SRE (Marta Ruiz) for permission to run fault injection on perf cluster and to schedule maintenance windows. For trace storage use the perf-bucket/test-runs prefix.
